claim: The S3 User Guide says S3 Replication Time Control replicates most uploaded objects in seconds, and 99.9 percent of those objects within 15 minutes.
question: According to the S3 User Guide, what share of objects does S3 RTC replicate within 15 minutes?

qualifiers.scope: per replication rule with S3 RTC enabled

evidence.quote: S3 RTC replicates most objects that you upload to Amazon S3 in seconds, and 99.9 percent of those objects within 15 minutes.

note: The S3 FAQ facts (s3-faq-rtc-15-minutes, s3-replication-time-control-15-minutes) say 'designed to replicate 99.99% of objects within 15 minutes' with an SLA of 99.9%; this User Guide page states 99.9 percent. Both are recorded as the sources say; a writer should teach the SLA figure (99.9%) and treat 99.99% as the design target.

claim: The S3 RTC SLA does not apply during periods when the S3 request-rate performance guidelines are exceeded, or when the replication data transfer rate exceeds the default 1 gigabit per second (Gbps) quota.
question: When does the S3 Replication Time Control SLA not apply?

qualifiers.condition: the transfer rate quota can be raised

evidence.quote: The S3 RTC service level agreement (SLA) doesn't apply to time periods when Amazon S3 performance guidelines on requests per second are exceeded.
The S3 RTC SLA also doesn't apply during time periods where your replication data transfer rate exceeds the default 1 gigabit per second (Gbps) quota.

claim: In an S3 RTC replication rule, the EventThreshold minutes and the ReplicationTime minutes can only be set to 15.
question: What values can the S3 RTC ReplicationTime and EventThreshold minutes take?

evidence.quote: `Metrics:EventThreshold:Minutes` and `ReplicationTime:Time:Minutes` can only have `15` as a valid value.

claim: Replication metrics and replication events become available within 15 minutes of enabling S3 RTC; enabling S3 RTC also enables S3 Replication metrics on the rule.
question: How soon after enabling S3 RTC are replication metrics and events available?

values.display: within 15 minutes of enabling S3 RTC
values.spoken: within fifteen minutes of enabling S3 RTC

evidence.quote: Replication metrics are available within 15 minutes of enabling S3 RTC.
Replication events are available within 15 minutes of enabling S3 RTC.
When you enable S3 RTC, S3 Replication metrics are also enabled on your replication rule.

claim: For each replicated object, S3 replication makes up to 5 GET/HEAD requests and 1 PUT request to the source bucket and 1 PUT request to each destination bucket, and these count toward the request-rate guidelines; you pay for only 1 PUT request per object replicated.
question: How many requests does S3 replication make per replicated object, and how many are billed?

values.spoken: up to five GET or HEAD requests
one PUT request per object replicated

evidence.quote: For each object replicated, Amazon S3 replication makes up to five `GET`/`HEAD` requests and one `PUT` request to the source bucket, and one `PUT` request to each destination bucket.

Your total request rate including the requests that Amazon S3 replication makes on your behalf must be within the Amazon S3 request rate guidelines for both the replication source and destination buckets.
You incur costs for only one `PUT` request per object replicated.

claim: When replicating SSE-KMS encrypted objects, AWS KMS requests-per-second quotas apply to the requests S3 replication makes on your behalf, and KMS can throttle them with a ThrottlingException.
question: Which quota can throttle replication of SSE-KMS encrypted objects?

values.display: AWS KMS requests per second quotas apply
values.spoken: AWS KMS requests per second quotas apply

evidence.quote: When you replicate objects that are encrypted with server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys (SSE-KMS), AWS KMS requests per second quotas apply.
The AWS KMS request rate quota applies to requests that you make directly and to requests made by Amazon S3 replication on your behalf.

claim: By default an account can create up to 10,000 general purpose buckets, and any customer can request a quota increase up to 1 million buckets.
question: How far can the general purpose bucket quota be raised above the default?

qualifiers.condition: by quota increase request in Service Quotas

evidence.quote: By default, you can create up to 10,000 general purpose buckets per AWS account.
Additionally, any customer can request a quota increase up to 1 million buckets.

note: Repair of the 2026-10-10 rejection of s3-bucket-quota-max-increase (M4 on the What's New quote). The 1 million ceiling is stated only in the What's New item (2024-11-14); the post page itself is blocked by robots.txt, so the API listing snapshot is the evidence. The old value (100) is carried by s3-bucket-quota-change-note.

claim: Accounts with an approved general purpose bucket quota above 10,000 must send paginated ListBuckets requests; unpaginated ListBuckets requests are rejected for them.
question: What happens to unpaginated ListBuckets requests in an account whose bucket quota is above 10,000?

qualifiers.condition: approved general purpose bucket quota above 10,000

evidence.quote: All unpaginated `ListBuckets` requests will be rejected for AWS accounts with a general purpose bucket quota greater than 10,000.

claim: Only some S3 quotas can be increased, and increases are not granted immediately; one may take a couple of days to become effective.
question: Can every S3 quota be increased, and how fast does an increase take effect?

values.display: may take a couple of days
values.spoken: may take a couple of days

evidence.quote: You can request an increase for some quotas, but not all quotas can be increased. These increases are not granted immediately, so it may take a couple of days for your increase to become effective.
